title: the 3 (children / the children)
subtitle: children / the children
summary: Leave out the when you talk about things or people in general, and use the when you mean specific things or people.

lesson.heading: Things and people in general: no the
lesson.text: When we are talking about things or people in general, we do not use the. Dogs means dogs in general, not a specific group of dogs. The same is true for jobs, hobbies, abstract ideas, kinds of food, sports and school subjects.

examples.text: Do you know anybody who collects **stamps**?
**Life** has changed a lot in the last thirty years.
Do you like **classical music** / **Chinese food** / **fast cars**?
My favourite subject at school was **history** / **physics** / **English**.

lesson.heading: most people, most shops
lesson.text: We say most people / most shops / most big cities etc. - not the most.

left.label: In general (without the)
examples: **Children** learn from playing. (= children in general)
**English people** drink a lot of tea. (= English people in general)

right.label: Specific people or things (with the)
examples: We took **the children** to the zoo. (= a specific group, perhaps the speaker's children)
The film wasn't very good, but I liked **the music**. (= the music in the film)
All **the cars** in this car park belong to people who work here.
Can you pass **the sugar**, please? (= the sugar on the table)
**The English people** I know drink a lot of tea. (= only the English people I know)

lesson.heading: Not always clear-cut
lesson.text: The difference between 'something in general' and 'something specific' is not always very clear. A phrase like people who say what they think or strong black coffee is narrower than all people or all coffee, but it is still a general idea, so there is no the.

examples.text: I like working with **people who say what they think**.
examples.note: not all people, but still a general idea

examples.text: I like **the people** I work with.

examples.note: not all coffee, but still a general idea

examples.text: **The coffee** we had after dinner wasn't very good.

lesson.heading: Quick guide
rows: A whole class of things or people
Sugar isn't very good for you.
A specific example the listener can identify
Can you pass the sugar, please?

lesson.text: If you can add 'in general' after the noun and the meaning stays the same, leave out the. If you mean 'the ones we both know about', use the.

exercises.prompt: Look at ___ on that tree. They're very big.
exercises.explanation: We mean specific apples - the ones on that tree - so the apples.
Spiders in general, so no the.

exercises.prompt: A vegetarian is somebody who doesn't eat ___.
exercises.explanation: Meat in general, so no the.

exercises.statement: It annoys me when the people throw rubbish on the ground.
exercises.explanation: It annoys me when people throw rubbish on the ground. We mean people in general, so no the.

exercises.prompt: The test wasn't hard. I answered ___ without difficulty.
exercises.explanation: Specific questions - the ones in the test - so the questions.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the word or phrase that completes it. Notice which ones need the.

pairs.left: Do you know ... who live in the flat next to yours?
... is the study of plants and animals.
It's better to tell the truth. Telling ... often causes problems.
We couldn't find anywhere to stay in the town. ... were all full.
Don't sit on ... It's wet after the rain.
You need ... to teach young children.

exercises.prompt: A pacifist is somebody who is against ___.
exercises.explanation: War in general, not one specific war, so no the.

exercises.statement: The First World War began in 1914 and ended in 1918.
exercises.explanation: Correct. This is one specific war with a name, so we use the.

exercises.prompt: Does the word in brackets need the in the gap? Sort the sentences.

items.text: Steve is very good at telling ... (stories)
I can't sing this song. I don't know ... (words)
Don't stay in that hotel. It's noisy and ... are very small. (rooms)
I don't have a car, so I use ... most of the time. (public transport)
... is strange sometimes. Some very strange things happen. (life)
We enjoyed our holiday. ... was good. (weather)
I don't like ... with unhappy endings. (films)

exercises.prompt: Don't swim in this pool. ___ doesn't look very clean.
exercises.explanation: Specific water - the water in this pool - so The water.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a general statement about two jobs.
exercises.answer: Doctors are usually paid more than teachers.
exercises.explanation: Doctors and teachers in general, so no the.

exercises.prompt: All ___ on the top shelf belong to me.
exercises.explanation: Specific books - the ones on the top shelf - so All the books.
